messages.subject: Re: How to keep track to the source file of each concordance
messages.subject_clean: How to keep track to the source file of each concordance
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

A while ago, I asked for help because I needed to identify in my
output file which file each concordance had been taken from. Then
Stefan suggested something and that's how my script looks like now:

as.character(mapply(paste, paste("File_", 1:length(all.in.one.list),
sep=""), all.in.one.list, sep="\t"))-> lings_file

lings_file2<-unlist(strsplit(lings_file,"\\W+"))
lings_file3<-unlist(strsplit(lings_file2," +"))
(matches.in.lings_file<-grep("(rmos$)", lings_file3, ignore.case=T))
output.file= file.choose()
for(i in matches.in.all.lings)
{ cat(lings_file3[max(0,i-10):max(0,i-1)], "\t", lings_file3[i],
"\t",
lings_file3[(i+1):min(i+10,length(lings_file3)+1)], "\n",
file=output.file, append=T)}
:-)

Now my data looks like this in the spreadsheet:

"File_1 t Por isso brigamos para /venceRMOS/       o Grupo A"
"File_2 tNós não vamos nos      /deteRMOS/       nisso"

So, the problem is: The file name gets pasted in a way that doesn't
allow me to sort correctly in the spreadsheet. Sometimes the name is
right next to the node, what messes up the sorting. I'd like the file
name to be in a separate columm, but then Stefan explained that:

> :-) well, that's because this line uses the tabs u put in there for strsplit:
>
> lings_file2<-unlist(strsplit(lings_file,"\\W+"))
>
> A tab is an example of \\W ...

What should I do to have the name pasted in a separate columm instead?
Does anyone have any suggestions?

Thanks in advance!
Fernanda

messages.body_plain:
Same problem as before:

> as.character(mapply(paste, paste("File_", 1:length(all.in.one.list), sep=""), all.in.one.list, sep="\t"))-> lings_file

this line inserts a tab stop and a tab but ...

> lings_file2<-unlist(strsplit(lings_file,"\\W+"))
... this line uses non-word characters (i.e., also tab stops) to split
up stuff, hence the tabs are gone.

Without (made-up) example data, it's more difficult to give advice but
it seems like you want to cat the file name first:

{ cat(FILENAME, "\t", lings_file3[max(0,i-10):max(0,i-1)], "\t",

lings_file3[i], "\t",
lings_file3[(i+1):min(i+10,length(lings_file3)+1)], "\n",
file=output.file, append=T) }

HTH,

STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries

messages.subject: RE: [CorpLing with R] using gsubfn on Mac OS
messages.subject_clean: [CorpLing with R] using gsubfn on Mac OS
messages.body_plain:
I've used different recent versions of R on Macs and have not had a problem using the gsubfn library, including strapply. But, yes, on a Mac the Tcl/Tk component is a separate installation, unlike on Windows. The installation is available at

http://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/tools/

John

________________________________________

I have been having difficulty getting the 'strapply' function from
gsubfn to work on my Mac OS.

The function works fine for me on Windows, but when I try to use it in
Mac, it gives the message 'Loading Tcl/Tk interface...' then goes back
to '>' to prompt more input. If the function is entered again, the
console freezes.

I guess there must be something I've missed here. Any ideas?
